chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Do not make permissible for yourself any game while you are in the state of Ihram, nor (make it permissible) while you are not in Ihram within the Sanctuary (Haram). Do not point it out to one who is permitted to hunt, nor to one who is prohibited, so that they may hunt it. And do not indicate it to it, so that it may be made permissible due to you, for therein is a ransom (fidyah) for the one who deliberately targets it.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules of hunting for those in Ihram and those outside the Haram boundaries?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) expands the prohibition of hunting to include not only the direct act but also indirect causation, such as signaling game to others, emphasizing that the liability for fidyah applies to the one who deliberately facilitates the hunt. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intentionality and the broader scope of ritual sanctity within the Haram boundaries, ensuring that the spiritual state of Ihram or the physical sanctity of the area is preserved from any form of exploitation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is nothing Permissible from the hunting, and you are in Ihraam, nor if you are not in Ihraam, inside the Harram, nor can you point towards it, whether you are in Ihraam or not, so that it can be hunted, not can you mention it so that it would be permissible (to be hunted) due to you, for therein is a ransom for the one who deliberates to it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Hunting in al-Haram (the sacred area) is not lawful, whether you are in the state of Ihram or not. You cannot show a prey to one who is not in the state of Ihram or is in the state of Ihram so they can hunt it. You cannot point out it so that it is hunted because of you. There is a ransom for it on one who violates the rule knowingly.”’
